input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: § 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment on Customer expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — squarely the playbook's walk-away position, and well short of the fallback (single 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up rather than penalty). The Customer-favourable provisions elsewhere (§ 9.4 convenience termination on 30 days' notice; § 12.3 acknowledgement that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment; § 7.1 bar on unidentified minimum-use charges) contradict § 2.1, and the Agreement contains no order-of-precedence clause to resolve the conflict, so § 2.1 could be read to override them. We therefore replace the commitment with pay-for-use language, which reaches the preferred position and is consistent with the rest of the bargain; the 12-month reducible commitment with true-up is offered as a fallback in the comment.

ops.oldText: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: Customer has no minimum purchase commitment and will pay only for Services used or ordered under an Order Form during the applicable term.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment, as our playbook does not permit multi-year minimum commitments with no reduction or termination right; this also aligns § 2.1 with the convenience-termination right in § 9.4 and the no-minimum-volume acknowledgement in § 12.3. If a commitment is commercially essential, we can accept one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice and settled by true-up rather than penalty.
proposal.summary: Delete take-or-pay commitment; pay only for Services used or ordered.
